description: FAQ accordion using native HTML details/summary elements. Zero JavaScript required. Each item has a question and an HTML answer. Emits a FAQPage JSON-LD structured-data block alongside the visible markup, zero-config with no toggle: an entry whose question or answer is empty is skipped, as is one whose value is damaged (a non-scalar, or an entry that is not an object), and no block is emitted at all when no entry survives. REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, motion — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors). Also becomes the component's stable id.

title.description: Section heading displayed above the FAQ list.

title_accent.description: Optional exact substring of title to render in an accent color. Must match title exactly (case-sensitive) or it is ignored.

eyebrow.description: Optional short kicker/label rendered as a pill above the title.

items.description: Array of FAQ items. Each item: { question: string, answer: string (HTML allowed) }.

question.description: The question text shown in the accordion summary. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

answer.description: The answer body. Rich HTML (sanitized via wp_kses_post): block-level markup, lists, and links are allowed.

retired_props._note: Props this component declared on 1.x that the v2 rebuild retired (#1046). Each value names the v2 surface that replaced it, so a refusal can offer a route instead of a list of live prop names. Guarded by SchemaValidationTest, which fails in BOTH directions: a key here that still exists in props, or a route naming a role this component does not declare, is a test failure rather than a message that lies.
retired_props.theme: the `_band` role — and it takes MORE than a background, which is why the route names three groups rather than one. MEASURED, all three values, before the prop went: `default` painted `@color-surface` with NO border on any edge; `muted` painted the same fill PLUS a 1px solid `@color-border` rule top and bottom (it emitted the legacy `faq--dark` class, #570 DG-4); `inverted` swapped the fill for `@color-bg-inverted` and re-coloured the heading to `@color-bg`, leaving the question, the answer and the accordion items untouched because the items keep their own light fill. So: the tone is `background.fill`; the `muted` framing is `border.width-top` / `width-bottom` = "1px" with `style-top` / `style-bottom` = "solid" and `color` = "@color-border"; the `inverted` ink is `typography.color` on `_band` (the `heading` role follows it through `currentColor`). `dark` was NOT an accepted input value and is not part of this route: it was removed at #605 and `pp_theme_class()` clamped it to `default`.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. Set the band's own background here to make a dark or tinted band; the v1 `theme` prop is gone because a preset bundle of colours is exactly what the UDC expresses directly. THE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT v1's UNTHEMED BAND RENDERED, measured in Chromium at 375/768/1280 rather than read off the stylesheet: a surface fill and the shared band rhythm, with NO border on any edge. That last part is the difference from cta, whose `_band` draws a 1px rule top and bottom: v1's `.faq` declared no border at all — the framing rules belonged to `.faq--dark`, the retired `theme: "muted"` variant — so silence here is the faithful port, and the issue-332 border-immunity baseline in `pp-v1` has nothing of faq's to erase. A band background image is `background.image` (an attachment id) with `background.overlay` for the scrim, a capability faq never had on v1, where the component declared no `background_image` prop at all. SETTING `typography.color` HERE RE-INKS THE HEADING, AND THE HEADING IS NOT THE WHOLE BAND. The `heading` role follows this write through `currentColor`. The `question`, `question-open`, `answer`, `empty`, `heading-accent` and `eyebrow` roles do NOT, because each pins a measured v1 value, and a pinned role default is a DIRECT declaration that an inherited band colour can never beat. THAT IS EVERY ROLE ON THIS COMPONENT THAT PINS ITS OWN INK — `heading` is the only one that follows, through `currentColor`. (Fills and border colours are pinned in other places too, `item`'s among them, which is what the next clause depends on.) They fall into FOUR groups, three of which need a remedy and one of which needs nothing: `question`, `question-open` and `answer` sit inside the `item` panel, which stays light by default (see the `item` role); `empty` sits on the band fill itself and is the one a correct dark-panel write leaves behind (see the `empty` role); `eyebrow` also pins, but carries its own `@color-surface-accent` pill fill, so a dark band does not strand it and it needs nothing; and `heading-accent` sits on the band fill and is the one case that still CLEARS its floor — `@color-accent` on `@color-bg-inverted` is 3.23:1, which passes the 3:1 large-text floor because the heading's clamp floors at 28px, though it is an 80% cut in margin beside a 17.54:1 heading, so re-ink it deliberately rather than by accident. A dark band therefore costs this write PLUS one per role whose text it must reach.

eyebrow.description: The kicker pill above the heading. Measured byte-identical to cta's, section's and hero's eyebrow roles, and declared per-schema rather than extracted for the reason #1023 recorded: role declaration is data the engine shares, so a fourth copy of the same values is the contract working rather than duplication to factor out.

heading.description: The band heading (an <h2>). ITS `typography.color` IS `currentColor`, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE LITERAL v1 DECLARATION rather than a transcription of it. v1's rule was `color: var(--faq-heading-color, var(--pp-faq-heading-theme-color, var(--color-text)))` — a pinned literal, not cta's `inherit` — so the literally faithful port would be `@color-text`. The reason it is not: the only way v1 could render a dark faq band was `theme: "inverted"`, which supplied `--pp-faq-heading-theme-color`, and that prop is retired. Carrying the literal forward would pin the heading against the one band shape v2 newly makes easy — measured, `@color-text` on an authored `@color-bg-inverted` band is 1.006:1, invisible, the same defect #1026 shipped and corrected. `currentColor` in the `color` property is defined to mean `inherit`, so an authored `_band` -> `typography.color` reaches this heading (17.54:1 on that same band) and an authored value on this role still wins. It is IDENTICAL to `@color-text` on every band v1 could actually express, which is why only a dark-band read distinguishes the two. ITS WEIGHT AND LEADING ARE RESTATED and its family, tracking and `text-wrap` are not: the weight and leading CAME from `main > .faq .faq__heading` rules that existed ONLY inside the two media queries — which is why dropping them would have restyled every tier. Those rules are gone as of #1046; the measured values live here now, while the other three come from base.css's shared `h1`-`h6` rule and restating a global value would move it to the unlayered tier and beat that rule in every state.

heading-accent.description: The accented substring inside the heading, rendered only when title_accent occurs in title exactly.

list.description: The accordion stack. It owns the gap BETWEEN items; the column direction is layout geometry and stays in the stylesheet. The gap is the only design value on this element, which is why this role carries three groups rather than the usual six.

item.description: One accordion item — the <details> box. ITS FILL IS `@color-bg` AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE INK ABOVE IT. v1 deliberately kept items light even on an inverted band (the same choice grid makes for its cards), and that is why the `question` and `answer` roles pin their colours instead of following the band: on v1's own dark band their measured ink was unchanged, because the panel under them was still light. THE CONSEQUENCE IS YOURS TO CARRY IN v2: if you darken this fill, set `question` -> `typography.color`, `question-open` -> `typography.color` AND `answer` -> `typography.color` in the same write, or the text keeps a dark value on a dark panel. `question-open` IS THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO MISS AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: `question-open`'s default emits at `[data-pp-component="faq"] .faq__item[open] > .faq__question`, specificity (0,4,0), and an authored `question` colour emits at `[data-pp-band="<id>"] .faq__question`, (0,2,0) — so the default WINS and your resting write never reaches the open row. Measured: the band looks right until a reader opens an item, at which point the row reverts to `@color-accent` at 3.21:1 on a `#111827` panel, under the 4.5:1 AA floor for the 1rem/0.98rem weight-560 summary. `empty` IS NOT PART OF THIS TRIO and this write does not fix it: `.faq__empty` renders as a direct child of `.container`, on the band fill, never inside this panel — so darkening this fill cannot strand it, and re-inking those three cannot rescue it. Its own pinned colour is a separate obligation, recorded on that role. `overflow: hidden` is structural — it is what clips the open answer to this box's radius.

question.description: The <summary> row at REST — the closed state only. Its positional twin is `question-open`, which owns the expanded state, and the two are set together or not at all: a colour set here alone reverts the moment a reader opens the item, because the open role's selector carries one more compound and outranks this one. THE SAME RANKING APPLIES TO STATES, and it is the part that is easy to miss: a `:hover` or `:focus-visible` map on THIS role reaches a closed row and not an open one, because an open row is matched by a heavier selector. Set the state on `question-open` too when it must survive opening. Its size and leading are breakpoint maps and its weight is a flat 560, all three READ FROM THE BROWSER rather than from the stylesheet: v1's base rule DECLARED `font-weight: 600`, which never rendered, because `main > .faq .faq__question` OVERRODE it inside both media queries and the two partitioned every width. All three of those rules are gone from the stylesheet as of #1046 — do not grep for them. The pointer cursor, the marker suppression and the `transition` property list stay structural — no group can reach them. THE 44px TOUCH TARGET IS NOT IN THAT SET, and saying so would be false: it lives in the stylesheet inside `@layer pp-v1`, while this role declares `sizing`, so an authored `sizing` -> `min-height` emits UNLAYERED and outranks it at any specificity. Measured: `min-height: 12px` validates and emits, and the row really does render 12px. AND IT HAS TO BE HONOURED ON BOTH TWINS, THOUGH NOT FOR THE REASON THE COLOUR CASE GIVES: an authored `min-height` here DOES reach the open row, because an open `<summary>` is still a `.faq__question` and `question-open` declares no `sizing` default for the (0,4,0) selector to carry. What the twin costs you is a second AUTHORABLE surface — `question-open` declares `sizing` too, so a small value left on THAT role survives a correction made here. Do not reuse this role's colour ranking to reason about sizing; there is no sizing default on either twin. THE OBLIGATION, STATED THE WAY THE CONTRAST OBLIGATIONS ABOVE ARE STATED: a `min-height` below 44px on an interactive control fails WCAG 2.5.5. The default keeps 44px; you own what you author. That is the ruled posture for this surface (#1046) — the capability stays, the warning travels with it — and it binds `question-open` as well, which declares `sizing` too. Where the theme PUTS its 44px is a separate question and is not settled: measured, TWO roles declare a 44px default (hero's `cta-secondary`, nav's `logo`) and FOUR take it from a layered stylesheet rule (hero's primary `cta`, nav's `toggle`, and this role with its twin) — six tap targets, and an authored value outranks all six. Filed as #1058; do not read faq's placement as a divergence from a settled pattern, because there is not one.; `motion` -> `transition-duration` retunes the timing of that transition without widening what it animates.

obligations.why: `question-open` selects the OPEN row with a heavier selector and defaults to the accent, so it beats a colour set here the moment a reader opens the row. Set both.

question-open.description: The <summary> row of an OPEN item — the accordion's expand affordance, and the only role in this theme whose selector is an ancestor ATTRIBUTE state. Ruling A3 defers ancestor states as a value DIMENSION, so this is expressed the way nav's `link-current` expresses the current page: as its own role with its own selector, which is what the role-selector charset was widened for — at #994 for the child combinator, at #1046 for the two bracket characters. Measured with a real pointer click at three viewports: the resting `@color-text` becomes `@color-accent`, 5.43:1 against the item's own fill, and the disclosure chevron follows for free because it is drawn with currentColor borders — which is also why the chevron needs no role of its own: its INK is already authorable through this role and through `question`, and only its box and stroke are stated defaults. THE CHEVRON ITSELF IS NOT AUTHORABLE — it is a `::after` pseudo-element and ruling A3 defers those, so its 10px box, its 2px stroke and its 45deg/225deg rotation stay structural, the same classification nav's chevron rotation takes. A `sizing` WRITE HERE CARRIES THE SAME WCAG 2.5.5 OBLIGATION AS ITS TWIN: a `min-height` below 44px on an interactive control fails it. The default keeps 44px; you own what you author. This role declares `sizing` and carries no sizing default, so a small value left here survives a correction made on `question` — the two are separate authorable surfaces even though one element renders both states (#1046; placement across the theme is #1058). For COLOUR, though, the ranking runs the other way: this role's default outranks an authored resting colour on `question` (one more compound in the selector), which reproduces v1's positional-twin behaviour exactly: set both or neither.

answer.description: The answer body, revealed when the item opens. Its colour and leading are breakpoint maps and its size and weight are flat, every one of them measured rather than declared: v1 gave the phone tier `@color-muted` from an unscoped base rule and the two wider tiers `@color-text-secondary` from a rule inside `@media (min-width: 768px)`, which is the #1023 media-scope trap in its exact shape — carrying the desktop literal unconditionally would have restyled every phone render of the answer, and dropping the weight and leading with the rules that carried them would have restyled every tier. IT CARRIES NO MEASURE, deliberately: v1 declared `max-width: var(--faq-body-measure, none)` and rendered `none`, so the faithful port is silence. LINKS INSIDE THE ANSWER HAVE THEIR OWN ROLE, `answer-link` (#1069), AND THIS ROLE DOES NOT REACH THEM. The sentence that stood here until #1069 said an authored colour on `answer` "still wins, which is what a darkened item needs", and it was FALSE — measured, not reasoned: `answer`'s selector is `.faq__answer`, so a colour set here reaches an `<a>` inside it only by INHERITANCE, and base.css's `a { color: var(--color-accent) }` matches the anchor DIRECTLY. A direct declaration beats an inherited value whatever the cascade layer, so the unlayered authored block never enters the contest. The consequence was measured at 1280: the darkened-item write this schema prescribes (`item.background.fill` dark plus `question`, `question-open` and `answer` re-inked) left a link in the answer at **3.21:1** while the prose around it reached 14.33:1 — the same ratio #1046 fixed one row up, reported accepted with no findings. Set `answer-link` -> `typography.color` (and its `:hover`) on any darkened item. What remains TRUE of the old note is the reason `answer-link` declares no DEFAULTS: see that role.

obligations.why: A colour here lands on the wrapper and reaches an <a> inside it only by inheritance, while the stylesheet gives every anchor its own direct rule. Set the paired link role named above too, and its `:hover`.

answer-link.description: Links inside the rich-text answer (#1069). THIS ROLE DECLARES NO DEFAULTS, and the distinction that makes that the right shape rather than a hedge is worth stating exactly, because the reasoning that kept faq from having this role at all confused the two. RULE 2 FORBIDS A DEFAULT, NOT A ROLE. A default here would restate base.css's anchor values as an unconditional UNLAYERED declaration, which outranks the shared premium `main .btn:not(...)` rules for every band — repainting an author-written `<a class="btn">` inside an answer, which is the #545 nested-author-button defect reintroduced through a role selector, and `wp_kses_post()` admits `class` so that anchor is reachable. Measured on #1066's probe, such a button renders the full premium treatment today; a default here would take it. An EMPTY defaults block emits nothing at all, so there is zero cascade movement at rest and an unauthored prose link keeps the global anchor treatment exactly as v1 gave it. When an author DOES write here the value lands unlayered on `.faq__answer a`, including on an `<a class="btn">` — but that is a value aimed at "links in this surface", an address the author chose, not per-instance styling leaking somewhere nobody asked for (#1071 tracks that exposure, which this role joins rather than creates: section and cta have carried it since #1023 and #1026). THIS IS THE ADDRESS A DARKENED ITEM NEEDS: set `typography.color` here and on its `:hover` whenever `item.background.fill` goes dark, or the link strands at 3.21:1 while the prose reads 14.33:1.

empty.description: The "No questions yet." line a band with no items renders. ITS COLOUR IS A ROLE DEFAULT AND THE MARKUP LOST A UTILITY CLASS TO MAKE THAT TRUE. v1 rendered this grey by putting `text-muted` on the element, which hardcodes `--color-muted` from utilities.css in `@layer pp-v1`. WHICH WRITE THAT CLASS WOULD HAVE BEATEN IS HALF-TRUE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND WORTH STATING EXACTLY: a write aimed at THIS role emits unlayered and matches `.faq__empty` directly, so it beats the layered utility and the class never blocked it; a `_band` write reaches this line only by INHERITANCE, and an inherited value is used only when no declaration matches the element, so layer order never enters and `.text-muted` wins. The `_band` write is the one the class would have stranded, which is the dark-band case. footer's rebuild met the identical case at #994 and ruled it the same way: the template dropped the class so the role governs. `@color-muted` is therefore the measured v1 value carried as a default rather than a value left in the stylesheet, and an author who sets a colour here now gets it — which v1 made impossible not through that class but by declaring NO slot for this line at all, so there was no surface to aim at. READ THAT LITERALLY: it is the write aimed at THIS role that lands. THE `_band` WRITE DOES NOT REACH THIS LINE. A role default emits as `[data-pp-component="faq"] .faq__empty{color:var(--color-muted);}` — a direct declaration, unlayered — while `_band` -> `typography.color` emits on the band root and reaches descendants only by INHERITANCE, which a direct declaration always beats. Measured: with a `_band` fill of `#0f172a` and `typography.color` set light, this line still resolves to `--color-muted` (`#5e6677`) at 3.10:1, under the 4.5:1 AA floor for body text. So a dark band WITH NO ITEMS needs two writes, `_band` and `empty`, the same way a dark panel needs `question`, `question-open` and `answer` (see the `item` role — the open row is the one that is easy to miss). This is not a regression — v1's `text-muted` was stranded on `.faq--inverted` in the identical way — but v2 is the first version where the fix is one write away, so the obligation is named here rather than left to be discovered.
